sources: Fernandez Domingos & Han (2026) Table 1 model 6 (human beta and SE)
figA_human_reference.notes: LLM intervals are the 95% cluster-robust CIs already in the CSV, NOT the +/-1 SE bars the superseded scorecard drew. Human CIs are beta +/- 1.96*SE; the SEs are transcribed from the free-text description column of human_comparison.csv because no machine-readable human_se field exists.

figA_side_table.notes: E8 has no published human value (human_value is empty upstream). E8's LLM denominator is 67 players with a unique nearest-strategy label, not the full pilot roster -- ties are kept unlabelled by strategy_analysis/classify.py.

figB_surface_variants.notes: unsafe_rate intervals are cluster-bootstrap over 10 repetition blocks and are marginal: each variant was resampled on its own seed stream, so differences between them have no valid interval here and delta_vs_canonical is reported as a point value only.

figB_pooling_check.notes: Justifies pooling risk in figure B: between-variant spread exceeds within-variant spread across risk by roughly 15x and the rank order is preserved at all three risk levels.

figC_levels.notes: Cell mean is the mean of per-repetition rates (the CRN block is the sampling unit, not the decision). Two-player mechanism only; the N=3 run is excluded.

figC_paired_delta.notes: Paired within-model, between-opponent contrast on matched repetition blocks; 95% t-interval on the n=10 per-rep differences. This is the estimand the superseded sorted forest discarded by computing unpaired marginal intervals.

figD_position.notes: Ahead and Behind carry identical n by construction: every asymmetric round contributes exactly one of each. Five checkpoints, 10 CRN blocks each, all with SHA-256 run manifests.

figD_contrast.notes: Point contrast only: the upstream table publishes marginal intervals per position, not a paired interval on the difference.

figE_risk_response.notes: Two Gemini cells at risk 0.1 are saturated (20/20 player-races Unsafe), so every bootstrap resample equals 1.0 and the interval is degenerate by construction rather than precise.

figE_contrast.notes: holm_p_high_vs_low upstream was adjusted over a SEVEN-model family, not the five plotted; p-values are therefore kept out of the figure. The two smallest Wilcoxon p-values sit at the n=10 signed-rank floor of 2/2^10.

figF_rates.notes: Panel A: aggregate risk response of the two independent unseeded pilots.

figF_agreement_pooled.notes: Chance agreement and Cohen's kappa are computed here, not upstream. At risk 0.1 both runs are uniformly Unsafe so agreement is forced to 1.0 and kappa is undefined; the 65% figures at risk 0.6/0.9 sit only slightly above chance.

figF_agreement_per_seed.notes: Five shared race seeds per risk level; these are the clusters the pooled rate averages over.

figF_agreement_per_decision.notes: Every matched decision, so the figure can show the 222 units themselves rather than three summary heights.

figG_comprehension.notes: Wilson 95% intervals, absent upstream. The frozen gate applies to semantic accuracy only (>=90% overall, >=75% per domain); strict format validity is not gated, so the two metrics are drawn against different references. Rule recall's 0% strict rate is a true zero, not missing data.
